_comments: ORDER CONFIRMED -> SEND THE CUSTOMER THEIR DOCUMENT.
The one binding in the doc's table that can be built today, because it is the only one whose
Action already exists. 'Send Document' renders the confirmed order as its customer-facing bill,
resolves the billing contacts the order itself names, and refuses anything that is not a bill.
The other four suggestions — welcome sequence, fulfilment kickoff, provisioning notification,
save/win-back — have no Action to point at yet. A binding whose ActionID names nothing is worse
than an absent one: it looks configured.
WHY AfterUpdate AND NOT Before/Validate. Sending a bill is a side effect with an outside-world
consequence, and After* is fire-and-forget (queued, per MJ#3408). It is explicitly NOT part of
the all-or-none transaction ConfirmOrder guarantees, which is correct: a mail relay being down
must never roll back a booked order, and a booked order must never be un-booked because a PDF
failed to render.
WHY THE FILTER IS 'changed TO value' AND NOT 'is'. An order is saved many times after it is
confirmed — posting stamps JournalEntryID, fulfilment moves FulfillmentStatus, payments move
Balance. A binding on 'Status IS Confirmed' re-fires on every one of those saves and mails the
customer their invoice again each time. The transition filter is the difference between one
invoice and one per subsequent save.
SHIPPED AS 'Pending', DELIBERATELY. The engine only runs Active bindings
(GetActionsByEntityNameAndInvocationType(..., 'Active')), so this arrives wired and inert. Two
reasons: whether a company mails invoices automatically is a policy decision an operator makes,
not one a migration makes for them; and ScopeRecordID has to name a real Company row, whose ID
differs per environment, so shipping it Active and unscoped would mail every customer of every
company the moment it is pushed.
TO TURN IT ON: set ScopeEntityID/ScopeRecordID to the Company that wants it, then Status=Active.
RE-ENTRANCY IS ALREADY HANDLED. 'Send Document' writes delivery rows, and after-hooks are guarded
against an action's own write-back re-triggering it (EntitySaveOptions.OriginatingEntityActionIDs).
The seeded reusable filter from MJ#3408. Without it AfterUpdate fires on EVERY update.
If this lookup fails to resolve, the seed did not ship in your MJ release — do NOT drop the
filter and enable the binding anyway; an unfiltered send mails the customer on every save.
'Send Document' takes OrderID as its one required input. Entity Field, not Entity Object:
the action wants the id, and passing the live BaseEntity would serialize to {} — its fields
are getters — so the action would receive an empty payload with no error anywhere.
